topics.label: Introduction to Inflammation Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the lecture by framing the session's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and Damage Recognition Principles
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline how the innate immune system senses danger by detecting pathogen-associated and damage-associated molecular patterns using germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: PRR Families, Signaling Cascades, and the Inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific pattern recognition receptor classes, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of the inflammasome to activate inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Inflammatory Mediator Action, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Impacts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sentinel cells initiate the inflammatory response, coordinate leukocyte entry and egress across tissues and vessels, and risk causing systemic pathology when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and mediate long-term outcomes such as chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic of the next lecture.
